result.topic_en: Euler writes out the variation of the integral formula ∫Z dx when a new variable t is introduced, and deduces that for the variation to vanish the first integral part must vanish, giving the Euler–Lagrange equation N − dP/dx + ddQ/dx² − … = 0.
result.transcription:
VARIATIONVM TRACTANDI. 43

ſolutas, quarum aliae formulam $(\frac{dy}{dt})$, aliae hanc $(\frac{ddy}{dxdt})$; aliae vero hanc $(\frac{d^3y}{dx^2dt})$ etc. continebunt; dum contra omnes integrales eandem formulam $(\frac{dy}{dt})$ inuoluunt, quocirca variatio quaeſita formula propoſitae $\int Z dx$, ſequenti modo habebitur expreſſa;
$dt\int dx(\frac{dy}{dt})(N-(\frac{dP}{dx})+(\frac{ddQ}{dx^2})-(\frac{d^3R}{dx^3})+(\frac{d^4S}{dx^4})$ etc.$)$
$+dt(\frac{dy}{dt})\ (P-(\frac{dQ}{dx})+(\frac{ddR}{dx^2})-(\frac{d^3S}{dx^3}))$
$+dt(\frac{ddy}{dxdt})(Q-(\frac{dR}{dx})+(\frac{ddS}{dx^2})-$ etc.$)$
$+dt(\frac{d^3y}{dx^2dt})(R-(\frac{dS}{dx})$ etc.$)$
$+dt(\frac{d^4y}{dx^3dt})(S-$ etc.$)$
$+$ etc.

15. Quamquam hic meum inſtitutum non eſt methodum maximorum et minimorum pertractare, quoniam hoc alibi iam ſatis copioſe eſt factum; tamen hic praetermittere non poſſum, quin obſervem, ſi variatio formulae $\int Z dx$ euaneſcere debeat, quomodocunque etiam noua variabilis $t$ in calculum ingrediatur; id nullo modo fieri poſſe, niſi tota pars prima integralis ſeorſim euaneſcat, ex quo neceſſe eſt, inter $x$ et $y$ hanc aequationem conſtitui
$0=N-(\frac{dP}{dx})+(\frac{ddQ}{dx^2})-(\frac{d^3R}{dx^3})+(\frac{d^4S}{dx^4})$ etc.
et quia nunc variabilis $t$ nulla amplius ratio habetur, ſicque tantum vnica adhuc variabilis $x$ ſupereſt, clauſulis omiſſis hanc habebimus aequationem:
$0=N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}$ etc.
F 2 qua

items.quote: ſi variatio formulae $\int Z dx$ euaneſcere debeat, quomodocunque etiam noua variabilis $t$ in calculum ingrediatur; id nullo modo fieri poſſe, niſi tota pars prima integralis ſeorſim euaneſcat
items.english: If the variation of the formula ∫Z dx must vanish, however the new variable t enters the calculation, this can in no way happen unless the whole first integral part vanishes separately.
